source.label: Bob's Guide to Classic Pinball Machines

strategy.summary: Plunge the top saucer to light both captive-ball lanes. If the captive-ball rebounds are controlled, repeat either lit lane; otherwise keep sending the ball through the center spinner to the top saucer.

steps.text: Plunge the top saucer. It lights both captive-ball lanes and the pop bumpers.
If the plunge misses, hit the mushroom target beside an unlit captive-ball lane to light that side.
Shoot a lit captive-ball lane for 1,000 to 4,000, depending on how far the captive ball travels.
Keep repeating the captive-ball shot only while its rebound returns safely. If it does not, shoot through the center spinner and return to the top saucer.

alternatives.title: Top-saucer loop
alternatives.when: Use this when either captive-ball rebound is dangerous or a square hit rarely scores 4,000.

steps.text: Shoot through the center spinner to send the ball up top.
Collect the top saucer for 3,000 and continue through the upper playfield.

cautions.issue: Captive-ball shots can rebound toward a drain.
cautions.response: Test each side once and keep only the side whose rebound reaches a flipper or return lane.

quickInfo.name: Main route
quickInfo.summary: Plunge the top saucer to light both captive-ball lanes.

strategy.simpleOverview: Sky Kings uses the top saucer to light both captive-ball lanes and the pop bumpers. A lit captive-ball lane pays according to how far its ball travels, while the center spinner provides a safer return to the upper saucer.
strategy.overview: Sky Kings alternates between variable captive-ball scoring and a safer spinner-to-saucer loop. Plunge the top saucer to light both captive-ball lanes, then test a lit captive ball for value and rebound. Repeat it only when the return is controlled; otherwise use the center spinner to collect the saucer and relight upper play.
